interest: This file uniquely pairs high-level Allied policy directives with granular, firsthand field investigations by Wolf I. Ladejinsky and Jay Dixon Edwards detailing the grassroots frictions of rural land redistribution and compulsory food deliveries across multiple Japanese prefectures. Historians will find exceptional material on the dissolution of the authoritarian wartime Nogyokai, assessments of potential conservative political sabotage of reforms, notices sent to Japanese-American landowners in the Nichi Bei Times, and exhaustive administrative directories and statistical surveys documenting Japan's prewar and wartime agricultural experiment stations.
overview: This file documents the evolution, administration, and on-the-ground impact of agricultural policies in Japan from the final months of World War II through the Allied Occupation (February 1945–December 1949). Spanning 341 pages across State Department, SCAP, and military files, it traces the trajectory of agricultural policy from wartime intelligence gathered through POW interrogations to high-level diplomatic deliberations within the State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee (SWNCC) and the Far Eastern Commission. The collection bridges high-level directives with local realities through granular rural field surveys led by agricultural economist Wolf I. Ladejinsky and Foreign Service officers, detailing tenant land transfers, statutory cash rents, and compulsory food collection quotas. Additionally, it compiles exhaustive technical and statistical reports produced by SCAP's Natural Resources Section examining Japan's agricultural experiment station network, crop and livestock insurance, soil surveys, and the democratization of rural cooperatives following the dissolution of the wartime Nogyokai.
